documents.text:
RESEARCH MEMO

Matter: Sarin-Loyal Limited — Liquidation
Matter Code: INS/BLR/0002/2021
Client: Sarin-Loyal Ltd.
Author: Baghyawati Kade (Stenographer)
Date: 2021-11-14
Office: Bengaluru

QUESTION PRESENTED
Whether force majeure is available on the Liquidation documents in Liquidation, and how the triggering event interacts with delay and damages.

BACKGROUND
The following facts are presently on file:
- Financial creditor filed a Section 7 petition
The engagement concerns Sarin-Loyal Limited in India.

LEGAL ISSUE
Primary issues for research: Fair and equitable treatment, CoC commercial wisdom, Financial debt.

ANALYSIS
Indian contract law (and, where seated abroad, the chosen lex causae) requires a close reading of the force majeure clause against the factual matrix. 
The triggering event must be mapped to the clause language, notice requirements, and mitigation. Causation as against concurrent delay remains the usual battleground.
The claim quantum in play is the quantified claim (see claim documents). Forum: the contractual forum.

ARGUMENTS
For the client: Debt and default are established from the facility documents; CoC's commercial wisdom is largely non-justiciable.
Anticipated pushback: Claim is in the nature of an operational debt; Plan discriminates similarly placed creditors.

AUTHORITIES
Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016

CONCLUSION
On the present record, the force majeure case is arguable but fact-sensitive. Recommend preserving contemporaneous notices and independent engineer records.

Date: 2022-04-13
Office: Bengaluru

QUESTION PRESENTED
Whether force majeure is available on the Liquidation documents in Liquidation, and how the triggering event interacts with delay and damages.

BACKGROUND
The following facts are presently on file:
- Financial creditor filed a Section 7 petition
The engagement concerns Sarin-Loyal Limited in India.

LEGAL ISSUE
Primary issues for research: Personal guarantees, Financial debt, Fair and equitable treatment.

ANALYSIS
Indian contract law (and, where seated abroad, the chosen lex causae) requires a close reading of the force majeure clause against the factual matrix. 
The triggering event must be mapped to the clause language, notice requirements, and mitigation. Causation as against concurrent delay remains the usual battleground.
The claim quantum in play is the quantified claim (see claim documents). Forum: the contractual forum.

ARGUMENTS
For the client: Debt and default are established from the facility documents; CoC's commercial wisdom is largely non-justiciable.
Anticipated pushback: Claim is in the nature of an operational debt; Plan discriminates similarly placed creditors.

AUTHORITIES
Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016

CONCLUSION
On the present record, the force majeure case is arguable but fact-sensitive. Recommend preserving contemporaneous notices and independent engineer records.

Whether force majeure is available on the Shareholders' Agreement in Joint Venture, and how the triggering event interacts with delay and damages.

- 50:50 JV deadlocked over a capacity expansion

Indian contract law (and, where seated abroad, the chosen lex causae) requires a close reading of the force majeure clause against the factual matrix. 
The triggering event must be mapped to the clause language, notice requirements, and mitigation. Causation as against concurrent delay remains the usual battleground.
The claim quantum in play is the quantified claim (see claim documents). Forum: the contractual forum.

ARGUMENTS
For the client: Clause is enforceable as a bargained exit; Trigger was in accordance with SHA notice mechanics.
Anticipated pushback: Trigger was in bad faith to force a distressed sale; Clause is penal in the circumstances.

AUTHORITIES
Companies Act, 2013; Indian Contract Act, 1872

CONCLUSION
On the present record, the force majeure case is arguable but fact-sensitive. Recommend preserving contemporaneous notices and independent engineer records.

Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016

CONCLUSION
On the present record, the force majeure case is arguable but fact-sensitive. Recommend preserving contemporaneous notices and independent engineer records.

QUESTION PRESENTED
Whether force majeure is available on the Shareholder Dispute documents in Shareholder Dispute, and how the triggering event interacts with delay and damages.

BACKGROUND
The following facts are presently on file:
- Minority shareholders alleged exclusion from management
The engagement concerns Patla Corporation in India.

LEGAL ISSUE
Primary issues for research: Related party allotment, Valuation, Derivative claims.

ANALYSIS
Indian contract law (and, where seated abroad, the chosen lex causae) requires a close reading of the force majeure clause against the factual matrix. 
The triggering event must be mapped to the clause language, notice requirements, and mitigation. Causation as against concurrent delay remains the usual battleground.
The claim quantum in play is the quantified claim (see claim documents). Forum: the contractual forum.

ARGUMENTS
For the client: Allotment diluted minority without proper valuation; Conduct was burdensome and wrongful.
Anticipated pushback: Allotment was for bona fide capital raising; Minority had historically remained passive.

AUTHORITIES
Companies Act, 2013

CONCLUSION
On the present record, the force majeure case is arguable but fact-sensitive. Recommend preserving contemporaneous notices and independent engineer records.

Date: 2022-04-10

QUESTION PRESENTED
Whether contractual impossibility is available on the EPC Agreement in Construction Arbitration, and how flooding interacts with delay and damages.

BACKGROUND
The following facts are presently on file:
- EPC contractor delayed project completion
The engagement concerns Mittal-Rege Holdings in India.

LEGAL ISSUE
Primary issues for research: Contractual delay, Causation, Liquidated damages.

ANALYSIS
Indian contract law (and, where seated abroad, the chosen lex causae) requires a close reading of the contractual impossibility clause against the factual matrix. 
Flooding must be mapped to the clause language, notice requirements, and mitigation. Causation as against concurrent delay remains the usual battleground.
The claim quantum in play is the quantified claim (see claim documents). Forum: the contractual forum.

ARGUMENTS
For the client: Flooding constituted force majeure; Delay was outside contractor control.
Anticipated pushback: Flooding was foreseeable in monsoon geography; Contractor failed to mitigate.

AUTHORITIES
Indian Contract Act, 1872; Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996

CONCLUSION
On the present record, the contractual impossibility case is arguable but fact-sensitive. Recommend preserving contemporaneous notices and independent engineer records.

QUESTION PRESENTED
Whether force majeure is available on the Assessment Appeal documents in Assessment Appeal, and how the triggering event interacts with delay and damages.

BACKGROUND
The following facts are presently on file:
- TPO proposed an adjustment on intra-group management fees
The engagement concerns Sastry-Shenoy Pvt. Ltd. in Singapore.

LEGAL ISSUE
Primary issues for research: Arm's length price, Benefit test, Penalty exposure.

ANALYSIS
Indian contract law (and, where seated abroad, the chosen lex causae) requires a close reading of the force majeure clause against the factual matrix. 
The triggering event must be mapped to the clause language, notice requirements, and mitigation. Causation as against concurrent delay remains the usual battleground.
The claim quantum in play is the quantified claim (see claim documents). Forum: the contractual forum.

ARGUMENTS
For the client: Services were actually rendered and documented; Comparables must be functionally similar.
Anticipated pushback: No tangible benefit was demonstrated; Foreign AE comparables are unreliable.

AUTHORITIES
Income-tax Act, 1961

CONCLUSION
On the present record, the force majeure case is arguable but fact-sensitive. Recommend preserving contemporaneous notices and independent engineer records.

documents.text:
RESEARCH MEMO

Matter: Shanker Holdings v State Urban Development Authority
Matter Code: EMP/BLR/0023/2024
Client: Shanker Holdings
Author: Yashica Cherian (Senior Associate)
Date: 2024-12-22
Office: Bengaluru

QUESTION PRESENTED
Whether force majeure is available on the Wrongful Termination documents in Wrongful Termination, and how the triggering event interacts with delay and damages.

BACKGROUND
The following facts are presently on file:
- Employer sought to enforce a 24-month non-compete
The engagement concerns Shanker Holdings in India.

LEGAL ISSUE
Primary issues for research: Garden leave, Wrongful termination, Section 27 Contract Act.

ANALYSIS
Indian contract law (and, where seated abroad, the chosen lex causae) requires a close reading of the force majeure clause against the factual matrix. 
The triggering event must be mapped to the clause language, notice requirements, and mitigation. Causation as against concurrent delay remains the usual battleground.
The claim quantum in play is the quantified claim (see claim documents). Forum: the contractual forum.

ARGUMENTS
For the client: Post-termination non-competes are void as restraint of trade; Variable pay had accrued against published KPIs.
Anticipated pushback: Confidentiality and non-solicit remain enforceable; Variable pay was discretionary.

AUTHORITIES
Indian Contract Act, 1872; Industrial Disputes Act, 1947

CONCLUSION
On the present record, the force majeure case is arguable but fact-sensitive. Recommend preserving contemporaneous notices and independent engineer records.

Date: 2026-10-05

QUESTION PRESENTED
Whether force majeure is available on the Wrongful Termination documents in Wrongful Termination, and how the triggering event interacts with delay and damages.

BACKGROUND
The following facts are presently on file:
- CXO was terminated citing loss of confidence
The engagement concerns Shanker Holdings in India.

LEGAL ISSUE
Primary issues for research: Section 27 Contract Act, Garden leave, Variable pay.

ANALYSIS
Indian contract law (and, where seated abroad, the chosen lex causae) requires a close reading of the force majeure clause against the factual matrix. 
The triggering event must be mapped to the clause language, notice requirements, and mitigation. Causation as against concurrent delay remains the usual battleground.
The claim quantum in play is the quantified claim (see claim documents). Forum: the contractual forum.

ARGUMENTS
For the client: Post-termination non-competes are void as restraint of trade; Variable pay had accrued against published KPIs.
Anticipated pushback: Confidentiality and non-solicit remain enforceable; Variable pay was discretionary.

AUTHORITIES
Indian Contract Act, 1872; Industrial Disputes Act, 1947

CONCLUSION
On the present record, the force majeure case is arguable but fact-sensitive. Recommend preserving contemporaneous notices and independent engineer records.

RESEARCH MEMO

Matter: Bhatia Infrastructure Ltd. v National Highways Concessionaire
Matter Code: DIS/SGP/0026/2023
Client: Bhatia Infrastructure Ltd.
Author: Ekiya Suresh (Associate)
Date: 2024-01-11
Office: Singapore

QUESTION PRESENTED
Whether force majeure is available on the Shareholder Dispute documents in Shareholder Dispute, and how the triggering event interacts with delay and damages.

BACKGROUND
The following facts are presently on file:
- Minority shareholders alleged exclusion from management
The engagement concerns Bhatia Infrastructure Ltd. in Singapore.

LEGAL ISSUE
Primary issues for research: Valuation, Oppression and mismanagement, Derivative claims.

ANALYSIS
Indian contract law (and, where seated abroad, the chosen lex causae) requires a close reading of the force majeure clause against the factual matrix. 
The triggering event must be mapped to the clause language, notice requirements, and mitigation. Causation as against concurrent delay remains the usual battleground.
The claim quantum in play is the quantified claim (see claim documents). Forum: the contractual forum.

ARGUMENTS
For the client: Allotment diluted minority without proper valuation; Conduct was burdensome and wrongful.
Anticipated pushback: Allotment was for bona fide capital raising; Minority had historically remained passive.

AUTHORITIES
Companies Act, 2013

CONCLUSION
On the present record, the force majeure case is arguable but fact-sensitive. Recommend preserving contemporaneous notices and independent engineer records.

documents.text:
RESEARCH MEMO

Matter: Zacharia Corporation — CIRP
Matter Code: INS/SGP/0027/2017
Client: Zacharia Corporation
Author: Daksh Karnik (Counsel)
Date: 2017-01-25
Office: Singapore

QUESTION PRESENTED
Whether force majeure is available on the CIRP documents in CIRP, and how the triggering event interacts with delay and damages.

BACKGROUND
The following facts are presently on file:
- Corporate debtor disputed the existence of a financial debt
The engagement concerns Zacharia Corporation in Singapore.

LEGAL ISSUE
Primary issues for research: Financial debt, Fair and equitable treatment, Personal guarantees.

ANALYSIS
Indian contract law (and, where seated abroad, the chosen lex causae) requires a close reading of the force majeure clause against the factual matrix. 
The triggering event must be mapped to the clause language, notice requirements, and mitigation. Causation as against concurrent delay remains the usual battleground.
The claim quantum in play is the quantified claim (see claim documents). Forum: the contractual forum.

ARGUMENTS
For the client: Debt and default are established from the facility documents; CoC's commercial wisdom is largely non-justiciable.
Anticipated pushback: Claim is in the nature of an operational debt; Plan discriminates similarly placed creditors.

AUTHORITIES
Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016

CONCLUSION
On the present record, the force majeure case is arguable but fact-sensitive. Recommend preserving contemporaneous notices and independent engineer records.

RESEARCH MEMO

Matter: Chada-Kothari Pvt. Ltd. v Blue Oak Energy
Matter Code: BNK/SGP/0032/2017
Client: Chada-Kothari Pvt. Ltd.
Author: Tara Chaudhry (Stenographer)
Date: 2018-02-17
Office: Singapore

QUESTION PRESENTED
Whether force majeure is available on the Debt Restructuring documents in Debt Restructuring, and how the triggering event interacts with delay and damages.

BACKGROUND
The following facts are presently on file:
- Borrower missed two consecutive interest payments
The engagement concerns Chada-Kothari Pvt. Ltd. in Singapore.

LEGAL ISSUE
Primary issues for research: SARFAESI overlay, Event of default, Share pledge enforcement.

ANALYSIS
Indian contract law (and, where seated abroad, the chosen lex causae) requires a close reading of the force majeure clause against the factual matrix. 
The triggering event must be mapped to the clause language, notice requirements, and mitigation. Causation as against concurrent delay remains the usual battleground.
The claim quantum in play is the quantified claim (see claim documents). Forum: the contractual forum.

ARGUMENTS
For the client: Payment default triggered acceleration; Pledge can be enforced without court in terms of the deed.
Anticipated pushback: Default was technical and was cured; Enforcement would violate the standstill in the ICA.

AUTHORITIES
SARFAESI Act, 2002; Companies Act, 2013; IBC, 2016

CONCLUSION
On the present record, the force majeure case is arguable but fact-sensitive. Recommend preserving contemporaneous notices and independent engineer records.

documents.text:
RESEARCH MEMO

Matter: Ramanathan Infrastructure Ltd. — Loan Agreement
Matter Code: BNK/BLR/0034/2021
Client: Ramanathan Infrastructure
Author: Yatin Baral (Knowledge Manager)
Date: 2022-04-12
Office: Bengaluru

QUESTION PRESENTED
Whether force majeure is available on the Facility Agreement in Loan Agreement, and how the triggering event interacts with delay and damages.

BACKGROUND
The following facts are presently on file:
- Security package included share pledge and hypothecation
The engagement concerns Ramanathan Infrastructure Ltd. in India.

LEGAL ISSUE
Primary issues for research: Event of default, Share pledge enforcement, Intercreditor.

ANALYSIS
Indian contract law (and, where seated abroad, the chosen lex causae) requires a close reading of the force majeure clause against the factual matrix. 
The triggering event must be mapped to the clause language, notice requirements, and mitigation. Causation as against concurrent delay remains the usual battleground.
The claim quantum in play is the quantified claim (see claim documents). Forum: the contractual forum.

ARGUMENTS
For the client: Payment default triggered acceleration; Pledge can be enforced without court in terms of the deed.
Anticipated pushback: Default was technical and was cured; Enforcement would violate the standstill in the ICA.

AUTHORITIES
SARFAESI Act, 2002; Companies Act, 2013; IBC, 2016

CONCLUSION
On the present record, the force majeure case is arguable but fact-sensitive. Recommend preserving contemporaneous notices and independent engineer records.

documents.text:
RESEARCH MEMO

Matter: Seshadri-Kohli Pvt. Ltd. — Liquidation
Matter Code: INS/SGP/0038/2022
Client: Seshadri-Kohli Pvt. Ltd.
Author: Nathaniel Sami (Partner)
Date: 2022-08-02
Office: Singapore

QUESTION PRESENTED
Whether force majeure is available on the Liquidation documents in Liquidation, and how the triggering event interacts with delay and damages.

BACKGROUND
The following facts are presently on file:
- Financial creditor filed a Section 7 petition
The engagement concerns Seshadri-Kohli Pvt. Ltd. in Singapore.

LEGAL ISSUE
Primary issues for research: Financial debt, Fair and equitable treatment, CoC commercial wisdom.

ANALYSIS
Indian contract law (and, where seated abroad, the chosen lex causae) requires a close reading of the force majeure clause against the factual matrix. 
The triggering event must be mapped to the clause language, notice requirements, and mitigation. Causation as against concurrent delay remains the usual battleground.
The claim quantum in play is the quantified claim (see claim documents). Forum: the contractual forum.

ARGUMENTS
For the client: Debt and default are established from the facility documents; CoC's commercial wisdom is largely non-justiciable.
Anticipated pushback: Claim is in the nature of an operational debt; Plan discriminates similarly placed creditors.

AUTHORITIES
Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016

CONCLUSION
On the present record, the force majeure case is arguable but fact-sensitive. Recommend preserving contemporaneous notices and independent engineer records.

RESEARCH MEMO

Matter: Parsa Pvt. Ltd. v Silverline Pharma Ltd.
Matter Code: DIS/BLR/0042/2017
Client: Parsa
Author: Radhika Dugar (Senior Associate)
Date: 2017-04-28
Office: Bengaluru

QUESTION PRESENTED
Whether force majeure is available on the EPC Agreement in Construction Dispute, and how flooding interacts with delay and damages.

BACKGROUND
The following facts are presently on file:
- EPC contractor delayed project completion
The engagement concerns Parsa Pvt. Ltd. in India.

LEGAL ISSUE
Primary issues for research: Contractual delay, Causation, Force majeure.

ANALYSIS
Indian contract law (and, where seated abroad, the chosen lex causae) requires a close reading of the force majeure clause against the factual matrix. 
Flooding must be mapped to the clause language, notice requirements, and mitigation. Causation as against concurrent delay remains the usual battleground.
The claim quantum in play is the quantified claim (see claim documents). Forum: the contractual forum.

ARGUMENTS
For the client: Flooding constituted force majeure; Delay was outside contractor control.
Anticipated pushback: Flooding was foreseeable in monsoon geography; Contractor failed to mitigate.

AUTHORITIES
Indian Contract Act, 1872; Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996

CONCLUSION
On the present record, the force majeure case is arguable but fact-sensitive. Recommend preserving contemporaneous notices and independent engineer records.

Cross-ref (possibly wrong): see also MTR-2017-00040 internal KM dump.

RESEARCH MEMO

Matter: Andra Limited v Pacific Bulk Commodities
Matter Code: DIS/BLR/0043/2025
Client: Andra
Author: Radhika Dugar (Senior Associate)
Date: 2025-03-29
Office: Bengaluru

QUESTION PRESENTED
Whether force majeure is available on the EPC Agreement in Construction Dispute, and how exceptional weather event interacts with delay and damages.

BACKGROUND
The following facts are presently on file:
- EPC contractor delayed project completion
The engagement concerns Andra Limited in India.

LEGAL ISSUE
Primary issues for research: Liquidated damages, Contractual delay, Causation.

ANALYSIS
Indian contract law (and, where seated abroad, the chosen lex causae) requires a close reading of the force majeure clause against the factual matrix. 
Exceptional weather event must be mapped to the clause language, notice requirements, and mitigation. Causation as against concurrent delay remains the usual battleground.
The claim quantum in play is the quantified claim (see claim documents). Forum: the contractual forum.

ARGUMENTS
For the client: Flooding constituted force majeure; Delay was outside contractor control.
Anticipated pushback: Flooding was foreseeable in monsoon geography; Contractor failed to mitigate.

AUTHORITIES
Indian Contract Act, 1872; Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996

CONCLUSION
On the present record, the force majeure case is arguable but fact-sensitive. Recommend preserving contemporaneous notices and independent engineer records.

Author: Radhika Dugar (Senior Associate)
Date: 2020-09-08
Office: Delhi

QUESTION PRESENTED
Whether force majeure is available on the Competition Commission documents in Competition Commission, and how the triggering event interacts with delay and damages.

BACKGROUND
The following facts are presently on file:
- Connected persons included a consultant on the diligence team
The engagement concerns Kalla Ltd. in India.

LEGAL ISSUE
Primary issues for research: Connected person, Settlement regulations, Chinese walls.

ANALYSIS
Indian contract law (and, where seated abroad, the chosen lex causae) requires a close reading of the force majeure clause against the factual matrix. 
The triggering event must be mapped to the clause language, notice requirements, and mitigation. Causation as against concurrent delay remains the usual battleground.
The claim quantum in play is the quantified claim (see claim documents). Forum: the contractual forum.

ARGUMENTS
For the client: Information had become generally available through rumours and press; Consultant was not a connected person at the trade date.
Anticipated pushback: Timing of trades is highly proximate; Chinese walls were undocumented.

AUTHORITIES
SEBI Act, 1992; PIT Regulations, 2015

CONCLUSION
On the present record, the force majeure case is arguable but fact-sensitive. Recommend preserving contemporaneous notices and independent engineer records.

RESEARCH MEMO

Matter: Divan Ltd. v Kestrel Mining Co.
Matter Code: INS/SGP/0046/2018
Client: Divan Ltd.
Author: Tripti Yadav (Partner)
Date: 2018-10-06
Office: Singapore

QUESTION PRESENTED
Whether force majeure is available on the Personal Guarantee Enforcement documents in Personal Guarantee Enforcement, and how the triggering event interacts with delay and damages.

BACKGROUND
The following facts are presently on file:
- Financial creditor filed a Section 7 petition
The engagement concerns Divan Ltd. in Singapore.

LEGAL ISSUE
Primary issues for research: Fair and equitable treatment, Personal guarantees, CoC commercial wisdom.

ANALYSIS
Indian contract law (and, where seated abroad, the chosen lex causae) requires a close reading of the force majeure clause against the factual matrix. 
The triggering event must be mapped to the clause language, notice requirements, and mitigation. Causation as against concurrent delay remains the usual battleground.
The claim quantum in play is the quantified claim (see claim documents). Forum: the contractual forum.

ARGUMENTS
For the client: Debt and default are established from the facility documents; CoC's commercial wisdom is largely non-justiciable.
Anticipated pushback: Claim is in the nature of an operational debt; Plan discriminates similarly placed creditors.

AUTHORITIES
Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016

CONCLUSION
On the present record, the force majeure case is arguable but fact-sensitive. Recommend preserving contemporaneous notices and independent engineer records.

RESEARCH MEMO

Matter: Divan Ltd. v Kestrel Mining Co.
Matter Code: INS/SGP/0046/2018
Client: Divan
Author: Tripti Yadav (Partner)
Date: 2019-07-15
Office: Singapore

QUESTION PRESENTED
Whether force majeure is available on the Personal Guarantee Enforcement documents in Personal Guarantee Enforcement, and how the triggering event interacts with delay and damages.

BACKGROUND
The following facts are presently on file:
- Committee of creditors approved a resolution plan with haircut
The engagement concerns Divan Ltd. in Singapore.

LEGAL ISSUE
Primary issues for research: Financial debt, CoC commercial wisdom, Personal guarantees.

ANALYSIS
Indian contract law (and, where seated abroad, the chosen lex causae) requires a close reading of the force majeure clause against the factual matrix. 
The triggering event must be mapped to the clause language, notice requirements, and mitigation. Causation as against concurrent delay remains the usual battleground.
The claim quantum in play is the quantified claim (see claim documents). Forum: the contractual forum.

ARGUMENTS
For the client: Debt and default are established from the facility documents; CoC's commercial wisdom is largely non-justiciable.
Anticipated pushback: Claim is in the nature of an operational debt; Plan discriminates similarly placed creditors.

AUTHORITIES
Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016

CONCLUSION
On the present record, the force majeure case is arguable but fact-sensitive. Recommend preserving contemporaneous notices and independent engineer records.

documents.text:
RESEARCH MEMO

Matter: Vora Pvt. Ltd. v Pacific Bulk Commodities
Matter Code: ARB/SGP/0047/2019
Client: Vora Infra.
Author: Liam Koshy (Senior Associate)
Date: 2019-12-16
Office: Singapore

QUESTION PRESENTED
Whether force majeure is available on the Long-term Supply Agreement in Commercial Arbitration, and how the triggering event interacts with delay and damages.

BACKGROUND
The following facts are presently on file:
- Long-term supply agreement was terminated for alleged quality failures
The engagement concerns Vora Pvt. Ltd. in Singapore.

LEGAL ISSUE
Primary issues for research: Take-or-pay, Quality specifications, Wrongful termination.

ANALYSIS
Indian contract law (and, where seated abroad, the chosen lex causae) requires a close reading of the force majeure clause against the factual matrix. 
The triggering event must be mapped to the clause language, notice requirements, and mitigation. Causation as against concurrent delay remains the usual battleground.
The claim quantum in play is the quantified claim (see claim documents). Forum: the contractual forum.

ARGUMENTS
For the client: Termination was premature and in bad faith; Quality tests were not conducted as prescribed.
Anticipated pushback: Repeated failures amounted to repudiation; Consequential loss is excluded by contract.

AUTHORITIES
Indian Contract Act, 1872; Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996

CONCLUSION
On the present record, the force majeure case is arguable but fact-sensitive. Recommend preserving contemporaneous notices and independent engineer records.

QUESTION PRESENTED
Whether force majeure is available on the Commercial Litigation documents in Commercial Litigation, and how the triggering event interacts with delay and damages.

BACKGROUND
The following facts are presently on file:
- Long-term supply agreement was terminated for alleged quality failures
The engagement concerns Bera Holdings in India.

LEGAL ISSUE
Primary issues for research: Consequential loss, Wrongful termination, Quality specifications.

ANALYSIS
Indian contract law (and, where seated abroad, the chosen lex causae) requires a close reading of the force majeure clause against the factual matrix. 
The triggering event must be mapped to the clause language, notice requirements, and mitigation. Causation as against concurrent delay remains the usual battleground.
The claim quantum in play is the quantified claim (see claim documents). Forum: the contractual forum.

ARGUMENTS
For the client: Termination was premature and in bad faith; Quality tests were not conducted as prescribed.
Anticipated pushback: Repeated failures amounted to repudiation; Consequential loss is excluded by contract.

AUTHORITIES
Indian Contract Act, 1872; Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996

CONCLUSION
On the present record, the force majeure case is arguable but fact-sensitive. Recommend preserving contemporaneous notices and independent engineer records.

RESEARCH MEMO

Matter: Goel Corporation v Meridian Engineering Pvt. Ltd.
Matter Code: REL/DEL/0049/2020
Client: Goel Infra.
Author: Irya Sampath (Associate)
Date: 2021-04-19
Office: Delhi

QUESTION PRESENTED
Whether force majeure is available on the Lease Dispute documents in Lease Dispute, and how the triggering event interacts with delay and damages.

BACKGROUND
The following facts are presently on file:
- Developer proposed a joint development on peri-urban land
The engagement concerns Goel Corporation in India.

LEGAL ISSUE
Primary issues for research: RERA registration, Public purpose overlay, Family settlement.

ANALYSIS
Indian contract law (and, where seated abroad, the chosen lex causae) requires a close reading of the force majeure clause against the factual matrix. 
The triggering event must be mapped to the clause language, notice requirements, and mitigation. Causation as against concurrent delay remains the usual battleground.
The claim quantum in play is the quantified claim (see claim documents). Forum: the contractual forum.

ARGUMENTS
For the client: Unregistered family settlement does not perfect title; Metro alignment is a material planning risk.
Anticipated pushback: Long possession and mutation support marketable title; Alignment is only a proposal.

AUTHORITIES
Transfer of Property Act, 1882; RERA, 2016; Registration Act, 1908

CONCLUSION
On the present record, the force majeure case is arguable but fact-sensitive. Recommend preserving contemporaneous notices and independent engineer records.

Matter: Parmer Pvt. Ltd. v Pacific Bulk Commodities
Matter Code: REL/MUM/0050/2023

Author: Yash Pingle (Clerk)
Date: 2023-11-10
Office: Mumbai

QUESTION PRESENTED
Whether force majeure is available on the Lease Dispute documents in Lease Dispute, and how the triggering event interacts with delay and damages.

BACKGROUND
The following facts are presently on file:
- Municipality issued a stop-work notice mid-excavation
The engagement concerns Parmer Pvt. Ltd. in India.

LEGAL ISSUE
Primary issues for research: RERA registration, Marketable title, Family settlement.

ANALYSIS
Indian contract law (and, where seated abroad, the chosen lex causae) requires a close reading of the force majeure clause against the factual matrix. 
The triggering event must be mapped to the clause language, notice requirements, and mitigation. Causation as against concurrent delay remains the usual battleground.
The claim quantum in play is the quantified claim (see claim documents). Forum: the contractual forum.

ARGUMENTS
For the client: Unregistered family settlement does not perfect title; Metro alignment is a material planning risk.
Anticipated pushback: Long possession and mutation support marketable title; Alignment is only a proposal.

AUTHORITIES
Transfer of Property Act, 1882; RERA, 2016; Registration Act, 1908

CONCLUSION
On the present record, the force majeure case is arguable but fact-sensitive. Recommend preserving contemporaneous notices and independent engineer records.

RESEARCH MEMO

Matter: Nagi-Luthra Energy Ltd. v Meridian Engineering Pvt. Ltd.
Matter Code: REL/DEL/0051/2017
Client: Nagi-Luthra Energy
Author: Oni Virk (Clerk)
Date: 2017-12-12
Office: Delhi

QUESTION PRESENTED
Whether force majeure is available on the Lease Dispute documents in Lease Dispute, and how the triggering event interacts with delay and damages.

BACKGROUND
The following facts are presently on file:
- Developer proposed a joint development on peri-urban land
The engagement concerns Nagi-Luthra Energy Ltd. in India.

LEGAL ISSUE
Primary issues for research: Family settlement, RERA registration, Public purpose overlay.

ANALYSIS
Indian contract law (and, where seated abroad, the chosen lex causae) requires a close reading of the force majeure clause against the factual matrix. 
The triggering event must be mapped to the clause language, notice requirements, and mitigation. Causation as against concurrent delay remains the usual battleground.
The claim quantum in play is the quantified claim (see claim documents). Forum: the contractual forum.

ARGUMENTS
For the client: Unregistered family settlement does not perfect title; Metro alignment is a material planning risk.
Anticipated pushback: Long possession and mutation support marketable title; Alignment is only a proposal.

AUTHORITIES
Transfer of Property Act, 1882; RERA, 2016; Registration Act, 1908

CONCLUSION
On the present record, the force majeure case is arguable but fact-sensitive. Recommend preserving contemporaneous notices and independent engineer records.

RESEARCH MEMO

Matter: Dayal-Chauhan Energy Ltd. v National Highways Concessionaire
Matter Code: DIS/DEL/0052/2024
Client: Dayal-Chauhan Energy Infra.
Author: Vansha Thakkar (Knowledge Manager)
Date: 2024-11-16
Office: Delhi

QUESTION PRESENTED
Whether force majeure is available on the Contract Dispute documents in Contract Dispute, and how the triggering event interacts with delay and damages.

BACKGROUND
The following facts are presently on file:
- Parties disputed whether termination was lawful
The engagement concerns Dayal-Chauhan Energy Ltd. in India.

LEGAL ISSUE
Primary issues for research: Quality specifications, Consequential loss, Wrongful termination.

ANALYSIS
Indian contract law (and, where seated abroad, the chosen lex causae) requires a close reading of the force majeure clause against the factual matrix. 
The triggering event must be mapped to the clause language, notice requirements, and mitigation. Causation as against concurrent delay remains the usual battleground.
The claim quantum in play is the quantified claim (see claim documents). Forum: the contractual forum.

ARGUMENTS
For the client: Termination was premature and in bad faith; Quality tests were not conducted as prescribed.
Anticipated pushback: Repeated failures amounted to repudiation; Consequential loss is excluded by contract.

AUTHORITIES
Indian Contract Act, 1872; Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996

CONCLUSION
On the present record, the force majeure case is arguable but fact-sensitive. Recommend preserving contemporaneous notices and independent engineer records.
